title: Keep the club in a database

--- order: 7 unit: database optional: true title: Keep the club in a database summary: "Move the club's members from a CSV file into a SQLite database, so the app asks for exactly the rows it needs." language: python hook: "A file is read from the top every time. A database finds the rows you ask for." --- This lesson swaps the CSV file for a **database**, using the SQL from the SQL course (lessons 1 to 8 first, please). The app looks almost the same. Only three functions change: one opens the database, one reads the members with a `SELECT`, and one adds a member with an `INSERT`. The database is a file called `club.db`. It stays between Runs and reloads, like `members.csv` did. Open the **Files** tab to see it (it is not text, so it shows as a file you cannot read). One new detail: `group` is a reserved word in SQL, so the column is called `team`. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: club.py#predict check: type: predict q: "What does it print?" options: - "2" - "1" - "Ada, Sam" - "An error, because the table was never saved" actual: "2. Each INSERT adds a row, and COUNT(*) counts them. The database here lives in memory, so it starts empty every time." ``` ## Run ```step stage: run code: club.py#run try: { playground: python, starter: "club.py#run", height: 560 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I joined, pressed Run again (and reloaded the page), and the member was still there." } ``` Join a few members, then press **Run** and reload. They are still there, now stored in `club.db`. | Part | What it does | |---|---| | `sqlite3.connect("club.db")` | Opens the database file, making it the first time | | `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` | Makes the table once, and does nothing after that | | `SELECT name, team FROM members` | Reads the rows the page needs | | `INSERT ... VALUES (?, ?)` | Adds a member. The two values go in separately | | `conn.commit()` | Saves the change into the file | ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: club.py#run insight: "A database does the finding and the saving. The app asks in SQL, passes values with ?, and commits changes so they last." tasks: - check: type: question q: "A member joins but is gone after Run. The INSERT line is there. What is missing?" options: - "conn.commit(), which saves the change into the file" - "A semicolon after the SQL" - "conn.open()" - "A second INSERT" answer: 0 feedback: - null - "Python does not need one, and the INSERT ran fine." - "There is no such call. connect() already opened it." - "More rows would not save the first." explain: "An INSERT changes the database in memory. commit() writes it into club.db." - check: type: question q: "Why is the name passed as (name, team) after the query, not joined into it?" options: - "So what a person types is always a value and can never change the SQL" - "Because Python cannot join text" - "To make the query shorter" answer: 0 explain: "A name like Robert'); DROP TABLE members;-- is just a name when it is passed separately." ``` ### The missing line What makes a change last? ### Passing the values Where does the typed text end up? ## Modify ```step stage: modify try: { playground: python, starter: "club.py#modify", height: 560 } hint: - "The order is in the SELECT in load_members." - "Add DESC after ORDER BY id." check: { type: code, text: "Show the newest member first.", rules: { contains: ["ORDER BY id DESC"] } } smaller: check: type: question q: "Which query gives the newest member first, if ids go up as members join?" options: - "SELECT name, team FROM members ORDER BY id DESC" - "SELECT name, team FROM members ORDER BY id" - "SELECT name, team FROM members LIMIT 1" answer: 0 feedback: - null - "That is oldest first." - "That gives one row, and not the newest." explain: "The biggest id joined last, and DESC puts the biggest first." ``` Change `load_members` so the newest member is at the top of the list. ## Make ```step stage: make try: { playground: python, starter: "club.py#make", height: 560 } hint: - "Open the database, run SELECT COUNT(*) FROM members, and return the number as text." - "conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM members\").fetchone()[0] gives the number." check: { type: code, text: "Add a /count page that shows how many members the club has, using COUNT(*).", rules: { contains: ["/count", "COUNT(*)"] } } ``` Add a page at `/count` that says how many members the club has. Let the database do the counting. ```teacher summary: "Students move the club app from a CSV file to a SQLite database file: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, SELECT to read, INSERT with ? and commit to save." time: 40 timing: "Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify and Make 20 min" goals: - I can keep an app's data in a SQLite database file. - I can read rows with SELECT and add a row with INSERT and ?. - I can say why commit is needed. before: | This is an optional extension. Students should have done SQL lessons 1 to 8 (SELECT, WHERE, INSERT) and Keep the sign-ups. `club.db` is a real SQLite file kept in the browser with the course's other files, so it survives Run and a reload. It cannot be read in the Files tab. `group` is a reserved word in SQL, hence the column `team`. The Make step asks the database to count, which is the point: SQL finds, Python shows. running: - "Predict: it is the memory database, so the answer is the same every run." - "Run: join twice, press Run, reload. The members are still there." - "Investigate: take the commit line out and show that the member disappears. Ask why." - "Make: students reuse the db() helper. A function that opens, runs and closes is the pattern." stuck: - see: "A member vanishes after Run." ask: Is there a commit after the INSERT? fix: Add conn.commit() before conn.close(). - see: "sqlite3.OperationalError about a missing column" ask: What is the column called in the table? fix: The column is team, not group. group is reserved in SQL. - see: "The table already exists with the old columns." ask: Did you change the CREATE TABLE after the first Run? fix: Delete club.db in the Files tab and run again. stretch: Add a WHERE so a group page shows only one group's members. support: Give load_members and ask for the INSERT. leads: "Next: back to the Flask course, or on to the APIs lessons." exit: q: "Why does a web app use a database instead of reading a file?" a: "The database finds and changes just the rows needed, can be asked questions in SQL, and keeps working as the data grows." explain: | `sqlite3.connect("club.db")` opens a database file. `conn.execute(sql, values)` runs SQL, with `?` marking each value. `fetchall()` returns the rows. `conn.commit()` saves changes into the file. solutions: step-4: club.py#sol-modify step-5: club.py#sol-make struggle: "Remembering the order: open, run, commit, close. Write it as a four-line recipe on the board." class: activities: - at: end title: Spot the SQL minutes: 4 do: | Students colour the SQL inside the Python and explain which function reads and which function writes. ``` ```code club.py#predict import sqlite3 conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:") conn.execute("CREATE TABLE members (name TEXT)") conn.execute("INSERT INTO members VALUES ('Ada')") conn.execute("INSERT INTO members VALUES ('Sam')") print(conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM members").fetchone()[0]) ``` ```code club.py#run import sqlite3 from flask import Flask, render_template_string, request, redirect app = Flask(__name__) PAGE = """

Chess club

Members

    {% for m in members %}
  • {{ m["name"] }} ({{ m["team"] }})
    • {% endfor %}

Join the club

{% if error %}

{{ error }}

{% endif %}
""" def db(): conn = sqlite3.connect("club.db") conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row conn.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS members (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, team TEXT)") return conn def load_members(): conn = db() rows = conn.execute("SELECT name, team FROM members ORDER BY id").fetchall() conn.close() return rows def save_member(name, team): conn = db() conn.execute("INSERT INTO members (name, team) VALUES (?, ?)", (name, team)) conn.commit() conn.close() @app.route("/") def home(): return render_template_string(PAGE, members=load_members()) @app.route("/join", methods=["POST"]) def join(): name = request.form["name"].strip() group = request.form["group"] if name == "": return render_template_string(PAGE, members=load_members(), error="Please type your name.") save_member(name, group) return redirect("/") app.run() ``` ```code club.py#modify import sqlite3 from flask import Flask, render_template_string, request, redirect app = Flask(__name__) PAGE = """
